readings: For each media type with at least one track that has a non-null Bytes value and a positive Milliseconds value, calculate its bytes-per-millisecond rate as the sum of those tracks’ Bytes divided by the sum of their Milliseconds. Which media types have a rate above the unweighted average of these rates across all media types with a defined rate? Show each media type’s name, its rate, and the unrounded amount by which its rate exceeds that average.

For each media type with at least one track that has a non-null Bytes value and a positive Milliseconds value, calculate its bytes-per-millisecond rate as the arithmetic mean of Bytes divided by Milliseconds for its qualifying tracks. Which media types have a rate above the unweighted average of these rates across all media types with a defined rate? Show each media type’s name, its rate, and the unrounded amount by which its rate exceeds that average.
queries:
WITH rates AS (
    SELECT
        m.Name,
        1.0 * SUM(t.Bytes) / SUM(t.Milliseconds) AS rate
    FROM MediaType AS m
    JOIN Track AS t ON t.MediaTypeId = m.MediaTypeId
    WHERE t.Bytes IS NOT NULL
      AND t.Milliseconds > 0
    GROUP BY m.MediaTypeId
),
average_rate AS (
    SELECT AVG(rate) AS rate FROM rates
)
SELECT
    r.Name,
    r.rate,
    r.rate - a.rate AS amount_above_average
FROM rates AS r
CROSS JOIN average_rate AS a
WHERE r.rate > a.rate

WITH media_rates AS (
    SELECT
        mt.Name,
        AVG(1.0 * t.Bytes / t.Milliseconds) AS rate
    FROM MediaType AS mt
    JOIN Track AS t ON t.MediaTypeId = mt.MediaTypeId
    WHERE t.Bytes IS NOT NULL
      AND t.Milliseconds > 0
    GROUP BY mt.MediaTypeId
)
SELECT
    Name,
    rate,
    rate - (SELECT AVG(rate) FROM media_rates) AS amount_above_average
FROM media_rates
WHERE rate > (SELECT AVG(rate) FROM media_rates)
